title: Slicing and Dicing
description: Learn how to cut and crop your strings using indices and slicing!

content.value: Remember how lists have slots starting at index 0? Strings do too! You can grab a single letter from a string just like you grab a toy from a list.

word = "Python"
print(word[0])  # Prints P
print(word[2])  # Prints t

What if you want to grab a chunk of the string instead of just one letter? We use Slicing! We specify the start index, a colon `:`, and the end index. Python will slice the string, starting at the start index, and stopping JUST BEFORE the end index!

word = "Python"
# Slice from slot 0 up to (but not including) slot 2:
print(word[0:2])  # Prints Py

If you leave out the first number, Python starts at the very beginning: `[:3]` slices from slot 0 to 3. If you leave out the second number, Python slices all the way to the end: `[2:]` slices from slot 2 to the end!

word = "Python"
print(word[:2])  # Prints Py
print(word[2:])  # Prints thon
